newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT SEEN STAYING WEAK AGAINST DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT SEEN STAYING WEAK AGAINST DOLLAR.

text.p: The ringgit traded within a narrow range against the dollar in early Asian trading on Wednesday, but dealers said the dollar still has the strength to test higher levels.
"There was no big move this morning but that does not mean that it's over. The dollar still has scope to move higher," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.7750/80 to a dollar. It closed at 2.7645/75 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday, after hitting a new 42-month low of 2.7930 earlier in the day.
Dealers did not rule out a dollar rise above 2.80 for the first time since dollar/ringgit was officially floated in 1973.
"Dollar/ringgit could still reach 2.80 and probably going above that level," said another Malaysian bank dealer. "But I'm expecting some resistance at 2.7850."
Trading was expected to remain choppy due to thin volumes and wide spreads, dealers said.
